title: Induction on attn-only-2l (task-shuffled run): no behaviour to explain on the task as scored
label: null result: no mechanism claimed, not verified
behavior: Shown a random token sequence that then repeats, the model is supposed to predict the next token of the repeat (dataset task 'induction').
summary: On the task dataset the model is at chance against the scored targets (local-full, full precision): 1/64 top-1, mean target logprob -15.05 on clean vs -14.81 on corrupt prompts, no clean/corrupt gap. The investigation was stopped there, as the protocol requires; no circuit was searched for and verify_hypothesis was not run. Diagnosis: the targets the lab scores against are not the repeat-next tokens of the prompts they are paired with. The same target id is displayed as a different token string depending on the run, and targets passed explicitly are also reassigned across examples. On 8 prompts built so that every example shares one repeat-next token (which makes any permutation of targets a no-op), the model predicts it in 6/8 with logprob -1.60 vs -13.99 on corrupt. So the model appears able to copy, but the input-to-target relation this investigation measures is broken, and no mechanism claim is made.

claims.text: Against the task's scored targets the model does not perform the behaviour: top-1 accuracy 0.0156 (1/64), clean target logprob -15.05 vs corrupt -14.81 (local-full). Pre-registered prediction of >=0.5 accuracy was refuted.

Supplying the first 8 seed-0 prompts and their listed repeat-next targets explicitly still gives only 2/8 (local-full); the 'expected' strings shown differ from those in the task run for the same prompts, so scored targets are not tied to their prompts.

When all 8 prompts share the same repeat-next token, so target permutation cannot matter, the model predicts it in 6/8 with logprob -1.60 clean vs -13.99 corrupt (local-full). The failure on the task is therefore due to targets being decoupled from inputs, not to the model being unable to copy. This is an 8-prompt, single-token observation only.

limitations: No mechanism was investigated: no attribution, patching, attention, ablation or verification experiments were run (5 of 40 experiments used).
The claim that the model can copy rests on 8 hand-built prompts with one shared answer token (E0005); it is not a general accuracy estimate.
The target-decoupling diagnosis is inferred from displayed token strings and accuracies across E0002/E0004/E0005; the lab's internals were not inspected.
E0001 and E0003 are dataset listings (exploratory) and support no claim on their own.
open_questions: With correctly paired targets, what is the model's induction accuracy on a full dataset, and which heads implement it? This needs a run of the task without shuffled labels.
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: no mechanism claimed, not verified

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model performs the induction behaviour: on a repeated random sequence it predicts the next token of the repeat well above chance.

prediction.statement: Top-1 accuracy on the clean repeated sequences is at least 50% (chance is ~1/48262).
